children.name: pinneapple_simulation.vehicle.sim
children.doc:
Time-domain simulation of a wheeled vehicle on deformable terrain: multibody dynamics + Wong-Reece wheels.

Per step (``dt``, linearly implicit Euler, :meth:`MultibodyTree.step`):

1. Wheel geometry on the undisturbed surface: lowest rim point, terrain normal in the wheel plane, rolling
   direction, sinkage below the undisturbed surface; the soil memory ahead of the wheel gives its prior sinkage
   (multi-pass).
2. Slip from the wheel's angular velocity and its centre velocity, slip angle from the lateral velocity.
3. Wong-Reece forces (:class:`~pinneapple_simulation.terramechanics.WongReeceModel`): drawbar pull and normal force in
   the wheel plane, lateral force along the axle, soil torque about it; their derivatives with respect to the wheel
   velocities enter the implicit step, so millisecond steps stay stable while the wheels slip.
4. Vertical soil damping ``c = zeta 2 sqrt(k m)`` (``k = dF_z/dz``, ``m`` the vehicle mass per wheel) -- granular soil
   dissipates the energy of a bouncing wheel; the Wong-Reece laws are quasi-static and have none. ``zeta``
   (``soil_damping``) is a model setting, not a measured soil property (Chrono's SCM soil uses the same idea).
5. Rigid rocks: penalty contact (spring-damper, Coulomb friction) on the rim (grousers included).
6. Actuators: wheel speed PI with the motor torque limit, steering PD (heading hold), active suspension PD with a
   load-levelling loop (an assumed control law: the arm angles move to equalise the wheel loads), all torque-limited.
7. The terrain records the plastic trace of every wheel (ruts) and a grouser mark each time a grouser passes the
   bottom of a loaded wheel.

NASA VIPER (Volatiles Investigating Polar Exploration Rover) at full scale, from public figures.

Every published number used here is listed in :data:`VIPER_SOURCES` with its source. Numbers that could not be
found are marked ``"estimate: ..."`` with the reason; they were chosen to agree with the published envelope, track,
wheelbase and wheel size. The geometry is a parametric model built for this library from those numbers, not a copy
of any CAD model.

Caveat on the sources: from the environment this model was built in, the NASA documents could only be located with
a web search, which returned text excerpts; the PDFs themselves could not be opened, so slide or page numbers are not
given and the wording should be checked against the documents.

Wheeled planetary vehicles: a description (chassis + corner modules) with its CAD, the multibody model built from
it, and a simulator on deformable terrain with Wong-Reece wheels.

    import pinneapple as pp
    spec = pp.vehicle.viper()                                  # NASA VIPER from public figures (cited in VIPER_SOURCES)
    model = pp.vehicle.build_vehicle(spec)                     # multibody tree, masses and inertias from the CAD
    terrain = pp.terramechanics.terrain.DeformableTerrain(base, (-2, 10), (-3, 3), cell=0.01)
    run = pp.vehicle.VehicleSimulator(model, terrain, pp.terramechanics.get_soil("GRC-1")).run(30.0, speed=0.2)
    run.summary(); pp.vehicle.viz.animate(run, terrain, "run.gif", field="normal_stress")

Modules: :mod:`.spec`, :mod:`.viper`, :mod:`.build`, :mod:`.sim`, :mod:`.scenarios`, :mod:`.viz`. See

doc:
pinneapple_simulation — Physics simulation back-ends and data generation.

Sub-modules
-----------
numerical_solvers  (was pinneapple_solvers)
    PDE solvers (FDM, FEM, CFD): HeatConduction3D, NavierStokes3D,
    LidDrivenCavitySolver3D, ChannelFlowSolver3D, ElasticWave3D.
    Optional bridges to OpenFOAM and FEniCS. SolverRegistry, generate_pinn_dataset.
    CAD-to-CFD pipeline (CADToCFDPipeline).

particle_dynamics  (was pinneapple_dynamics)
    Differentiable particle / continuum dynamics: rigid-body (RigidBody,
    RigidBodySystem), MPM (MPMSimulator), SPH (SPHParticles). All in pure
    PyTorch for autograd compatibility.

external_solvers   (was pinneapple_integrations)
    External tool bridges: OpenFOAM case staging & field extraction, MATLAB
    engine wrapper, Modelica / FMU simulation (via fmpy / OMPython), FEniCS
    workflow. All optional — graceful degradation when tool not installed.

Integration helpers
-------------------
``simulate(scenario, ...)``
    Dispatch function: routes to the appropriate solver/simulator based on
    scenario string (``"heat_3d"``, ``"ns_3d"``, ``"mpm"``, ``"sph"``, …).
``generate_data(scenario, n_samples, ...)``
    Generates a dataset of trajectories using the matching solver.

Usage
-----
>>> from pinneapple_simulation import simulate, generate_data, HeatConduction3D
>>> output = simulate("heat_3d", t_end=1.0, nx=32, ny=32, nz=32)
>>> dataset = generate_data("ns_3d", n_samples=50)
